Utsab Sekh & Ors vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr on 20
February, 2023
Author: Bibek Chaudhuri

Bench: Bibek Chaudhuri
Form J(1) In The High Court At Calcutta
 Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction
 Appellate Side
Present :
The Hon'ble Justice Bibek Chaudhuri
 Cran 1 of 2023
 In
 C.R.R. 376 of 2023

Utsab Sekh & Ors.
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & Anr.

For the petitioner : Md. Asraf Ali Golam Mohiuddin, Adv.
 Ms. Puja Mondal, Adv.
 Ms. Sabnam Laskar, Adv.

For O.P. No.2 : Ms. Reshmi Ghosh, Adv.
 Md. Nazar Chowdhury, Adv.
 Mr. Soumya Sarkar Chini, Adv.
For the State : Mr. Saswata Gopal Mukherjee, Ld.P.P.
 Mr. Imran Ali, Adv.
 Ms. Debjani Sahu, Adv.
Heard on : 20.02.2023
Judgment On : 20.02.2023.
Bibek Chaudhuri, J.
Petitioners are the matrimonial relations of the opposite party No.2.

The petitioners have filed the
instant revision praying for quashing of all further proceedings in connection with G.R. Case No.244
of 2022 arising out of Naihati Police Station Case No.49 of 2022 dated 22nd January, 2022 under
Sections 498A/325/307/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act.
During the pendency of the instant revision, there was an out of Court settlement of the dispute between the opposite party No.2 and the petitioners.

Both of them have filed a joint petition for compromise, stating, inter alia, that the dispute between the parties have been amicably settled and the opposite party No.2 has been residing together with her husband and other matrimonial Utsab Sekh & Ors vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr on 20 February, 2023

1 relations at her matrimonial home.

On the last occasion, a Co-ordinate Bench has passed an order directing the petitioners to supply a copy of the application to the learned Public Prosecutor-in-Charge for obtaining a police report to ascertain as to whether the compromise petition is filed voluntarily and free from threat, coercion and undue influence.
The police submitted a report to the effect that the de-facto complainant has compromised the case voluntarily on her own accord.

In view of such circumstances and on perusal of the record, there having no ingredient of offence under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code, I am inclined to quash the criminal proceeding instituted against the petitioners at the instance of the opposite party on the basis of the joint petition for compromise.
Accordingly, compromise has been accepted.
The further proceeding in connection with GR No.244 of 2022 pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rampurhat, Birbhum be quashed.
